name: AV1 Intel Arc QSV [Single ICQ, Seek-Heal Fallback V13 - REVIEW]
description:
Ultra-fast True Single-Pass AV1 Intel Arc Transcoder. Consolidates stream pruning, subtitle normalization, surround standardisation, QSV encoding, dynamic size guards, content-aware *ARR disk rescan, and Discord notifications.
V3: video timeline/decode checks, track preservation, storage and original guards.
V13: one global QSV ICQ encode, capacity-bounded source-video seek-heal remux when the AV1 output is not smaller, ISO refetch warnings, already-processed info notices, Profile 7 Level 6 fallback, live progress, and capacity-reserved RAM-first scratch.
Quality decision (2026-11-02): keep Arc QSV ICQ 22 provisionally. Live SDR VMAF v1 scored 96.62 (TV 3H) / 98.02 (phone 5H) on Sample 4K Film and 96.62 / 97.66 on Sample Anime Series; the Sample Anime Series full file fell 21.7%. A matched 20 s excerpt from an 80 GB HDR10 source scored 106.18 on Netflix’s 4K HDR model at ICQ 22, with static HDR metadata retained. This supports the tested SDR/HDR10 quality samples only. See QUALITY_DECISION.md before production.
HDR route smoke tests (2026-11-02): direct live Arc QSV runs produced clean-decode output for Dolby Vision P7 to static HDR10, Dolby Vision P8.1 to HDR10 with the Level 6 189/89 fallback, and HDR10+ to static HDR10 with dynamic metadata removed. Synthetic HLG retained BT.2020/HLG signaling. These are route and metadata checks, not matched quality checks or an end-to-end V13 Tdarr job. No genuine HLG or Dolby Vision 8.4 source was found among 212 named 2160p videos. Hybrid Dolby Vision/HDR10+ remains held. See HDR_LIVE_VALIDATION.md.
Codec handling candidate update: supported 4:2:2/4:4:4 formats are normalized to 10-bit 4:2:0; tagged SDR 12-bit is error-diffused to 10-bit. Non-direct-QSV sources use CPU decode while AV1 encoding remains Arc QSV. The local FFmpeg matrix is software-only; Arc validation of these broader codec paths remains pending. See CODEC_COVERAGE.md.
Failure notices distinguish malformed H.264 source scans from output subtitle packet mismatches and give next steps. Subtitle count mismatches keep the original and do not trigger automatic deletion or Arr refetch. See FAILURE_DIAGNOSTICS.md.
Recognized video bitstream errors from the pre-encode source scan, or strict output-decode failures independently reproduced by decoding the original video/audio stream, trigger an item-scoped Sonarr EpisodeSearch or Radarr MoviesSearch only after matching the exact file. The original remains in place; no file deletion, quarantine, monitoring change, or broad series/movie search is performed. Arr profile/upgrade rules determine whether a replacement is accepted.
Source precheck policy: tagged progressive SDR and verified static HDR10 videos longer than 16 seconds use three 5-second software-decoded samples at the beginning, middle, and end; sample intervals end at absolute timestamps to account for FFprobe seeking back to keyframes. HDR10+, Dolby Vision, HLG, untagged/ambiguous, short, partially tagged SDR, or non-progressive-tagged video keeps the full CPU source scan. If a sampled source/output timeline comparison fails, the flow fully scans the source and compares its complete frame count and timestamps against the candidate’s already-complete output scan; it proceeds only if that full comparison passes. Other encode/output validation failures keep the original unless every check passes. Sampled routes do not prove exact frame equality outside their three windows when the sample comparison passes.
Untagged SDR YUV handling: keep transfer, primaries, and matrix unspecified. If stream, decoded-frame, and MediaInfo range are all missing, assume TV limited range for supported YUV pixel formats; preserve known range and infer full range for yuvj422p/yuvj444p. Apply the resolved range tag to both AV1 encode and seek-heal remux. Conflicting or unrecognized ranges are held. This is a conventional assumption, not recovered metadata; it does not affect HDR/Dolby Vision.
Partial SDR metadata: a recognized BT.709, BT.601/SMPTE 170M, or BT.470 BG matrix can classify a source as SDR when transfer/primaries are absent and there are no HDR/Dolby Vision signals. Missing fields remain unspecified; a conflicting or unrecognized matrix is held. These inputs receive a full CPU frame scan and are rejected if frames signal PQ, HLG, or BT.2020.
Safety correction (2026-11-03): source field-order tags no longer trigger an output-only interlace check after a full frame scan. Non-progressive-tagged sources still receive the full decoded-frame scan, actual interlaced frames remain held, and output field order remains guarded. Reservation V3 records are scoped to worker host/PID namespace, heartbeat during engine work, and identify only their own scratch directory; dead or expired leases are reclaimed on the next admission. User cancellation can bypass downstream Tdarr cleanup and notification nodes.
